newsitem.title: USA: "Batman & Robin" wanes at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Batman & Robin" wanes at U.S. box office.

text.p: "Batman & Robin," the fourth installment in the lucrative Caped Crusader franchise, flew into the top of the weekend box office with $43.6 million, according to studio estimates on Sunday.
However, the take was only the third best of the four Batman movies, surpassing the $40.49 million opening of the first "Batman" from June 1989.
The record is held by "Batman Forever," which opened to $52.78 million in June 1995, while "Batman Returns" scored $45.69 million in June 1992.
Opening in second was the Julia Roberts romantic comedy, "My Best Friend's Wedding," which grossed $21.5 million for the Friday to Sunday period.
The Nicolas Cage airborne thriller, "Con Air," slipped a notch to third in its third weekend, with $10.2 million, which takes its overall total to $67.7 million.
Steven Spielberg's "The Lost World: Jurassic Park," also fell a notch, to fourth, with $8.0 million. After 32 days in release, the dinosaur extravaganza's total is $204.9 million.
Last weekend's number one, "Speed 2: Cruise Control," tumbled to fifth with $7.2 million. The 10-day total for the critically maligned Sandra Bullock action movie is $30.7 million.

"Batman & Robin" is released by Warner Bros, a unit of Time Warner Inc.. "My Best Friend's Wedding" is released by TriStar Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp.. "Con Air" is released by Walt Disney Co.. "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" is released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd.. "Speed 2: Cruise Control" is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp..
